title: Distance to bank as IV for savings rate

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS).
- Why: Account ownership (x) is likely endogenous (selection on unobservables such as financial savvy or access costs). Distance to the nearest bank branch (z) shifts the cost of opening/maintaining an account and thus affects x but should not directly affect savings (y) after conditioning on controls.
- Key assumptions:
  - Relevance: Cov(z, x | controls) ≠ 0. Households farther from a branch are less likely to own an account (expected negative first stage).
  - Exclusion: z affects y only through account ownership, not directly or through other channels after conditioning on controls (no direct effect of distance on savings).
  - Independence: z is as good as randomly assigned conditional on controls (income, education proxy), i.e., z ⫫ ε | controls.
  - Monotonicity: Increasing distance weakly reduces the probability of having an account for all households (no defiers).
  - SUTVA: No spillovers of distance across households.

Under these, the 2SLS coefficient on x identifies the LATE of account ownership on savings for compliers with respect to distance.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Packages
pkgs <- c("AER", "sandwich", "lmtest")
to_install <- pkgs[!sapply(pkgs, requireNamespace, quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(to_install) > 0) {
  install.packages(to_install, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
}
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# Read data
dat <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s20_data.csv")

# Basic summaries (optional)
# str(dat); summary(dat)

# Helper: robust SE coeftest extractor
get_coef_se_ci <- function(ct, name = "x", level = 0.95) {
  est <- as.numeric(ct[name, "Estimate"])
  se  <- as.numeric(ct[name, "Std. Error"])
  z   <- qnorm(1 - (1 - level)/2)
  ci  <- est + c(-z, z) * se
  list(est = est, se = se, ci = ci)
}

# 1) OLS benchmark: y ~ x + controls
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls, data = dat)
ols_ct <- coeftest(ols, vcov = vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1"))
ols_res <- get_coef_se_ci(ols_ct, "x")

# 2) First stage: x ~ z + controls
fs <- lm(x ~ z + controls, data = dat)
fs_ct <- coeftest(fs, vcov = vcovHC(fs, type = "HC1"))

# Extract first-stage instrument strength metrics
beta_fs_z   <- as.numeric(fs_ct["z", "Estimate"])
se_fs_z     <- as.numeric(fs_ct["z", "Std. Error"])
t_fs_z_rob  <- as.numeric(fs_ct["z", "t value"])
F_fs_z_rob  <- t_fs_z_rob^2

# 3) Reduced form: y ~ z + controls
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls, data = dat)
rf_ct <- coeftest(rf, vcov = vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1"))
beta_rf_z <- as.numeric(rf_ct["z", "Estimate"])
se_rf_z   <- as.numeric(rf_ct["z", "Std. Error"])

# 4) 2SLS: y ~ x + controls | controls + z
iv <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls | controls + z, data = dat)
iv_ct <- coeftest(iv, vcov = vcovHC(iv, type = "HC1"))
iv_res <- get_coef_se_ci(iv_ct, "x")

# 5) Endogeneity (control-function/Wu-Hausman): add first-stage residual
res_fs <- resid(fs)
cf <- lm(y ~ x + controls + res_fs, data = dat)
cf_ct <- coeftest(cf, vcov = vcovHC(cf, type = "HC1"))
p_endog <- as.numeric(cf_ct["res_fs", "Pr(>|t|)"])

# 6) Robustness A: IV without controls
iv_noc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = dat)
iv_noc_ct <- coeftest(iv_noc, vcov = vcovHC(iv_noc, type = "HC1"))
iv_noc_est <- as.numeric(iv_noc_ct["x", "Estimate"])
iv_noc_se  <- as.numeric(iv_noc_ct["x", "Std. Error"])

# 7) Robustness B: Winsorize y at 1% tails and re-estimate IV
winsor <- function(v, p = 0.01) {
  ql <- as.numeric(quantile(v, p, na.rm = TRUE))
  qh <- as.numeric(quantile(v, 1 - p, na.rm = TRUE))
  v[v < ql] <- ql
  v[v > qh] <- qh
  v
}
dat$y_w <- winsor(dat$y, 0.01)
iv_w <- ivreg(y_w ~ x + controls | controls + z, data = dat)
iv_w_ct <- coeftest(iv_w, vcov = vcovHC(iv_w, type = "HC1"))
iv_w_est <- as.numeric(iv_w_ct["x", "Estimate"])
iv_w_se  <- as.numeric(iv_w_ct["x", "Std. Error"])

# Print key results
cat("=== Main Results ===\n")
cat(sprintf("OLS (y ~ x + controls): beta_x = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            ols_res$est, ols_res$se, ols_res$ci[1], ols_res$ci[2]))

cat(sprintf("First stage (x ~ z + controls): beta_z = %.4f, SE = %.4f, robust F(z) = %.2f\n",
            beta_fs_z, se_fs_z, F_fs_z_rob))

cat(sprintf("Reduced form (y ~ z + controls): beta_z = %.4f, SE = %.4f\n",
            beta_rf_z, se_rf_z))

cat(sprintf("2SLS (y ~ x + controls | z + controls): beta_x = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            iv_res$est, iv_res$se, iv_res$ci[1], iv_res$ci[2]))

cat(sprintf("Endogeneity (CF residual) p-value = %.4f (H0: x exogenous)\n", p_endog))

cat("=== Robustness Checks ===\n")
cat(sprintf("IV without controls: beta_x = %.4f, SE = %.4f\n", iv_noc_est, iv_noc_se))
cat(sprintf("IV with winsorized y (1%% tails): beta_x = %.4f, SE = %.4f\n", iv_w_est, iv_w_se))

# Optional: flag weak instrument rule-of-thumb
if (F_fs_z_rob < 10) {
  cat(sprintf("Warning: robust first-stage F = %.2f < 10 (potential weak instrument).\n", F_fs_z_rob))
} else {
  cat(sprintf("First-stage appears strong (robust F = %.2f >= 10).\n", F_fs_z_rob))
}
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Positive 2SLS effect. Greater distance reduces account ownership (negative first stage). If having an account facilitates saving (lower transaction costs, commitment), the reduced form should be negative and the IV estimate of account ownership on savings positive.
- Magnitude: Moderate. Expect a meaningful but not huge monthly effect; in standardized units typical of this type of simulation, a 2SLS coefficient in the range 0.3 to 0.7 is plausible. If y is in USD for a lower-income sample, think on the order of tens of dollars per month rather than hundreds.
- Diagnostics: Expect a negative first-stage coefficient on z with a reasonably large F-statistic (preferably >10). OLS may be downward biased if more financially constrained households are both less likely to have accounts and save less, so IV > OLS is plausible. Control-function residual likely significant, supporting endogeneity of x. Robustness checks should yield similar positive signs and comparable magnitudes.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: IV/2SLS — instrument: branch distance; first stage: distance → account ownership (negative)
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Bank account ownership significantly increases savings
_ground_truth.main_effect: Having an account increases monthly savings by ~40% (IV estimate)
